title: Ten of the differences from Scheme that R7RS-small's cases show are departures, each for a reason Lion already has
context: The probes `r7rs-<section>-<what>` run 36 cases that R7RS-small settles, and in 20 of them Lion gave something else than Scheme. The rule `scheme-racket-semantics` names a departure as an exception in a decision, so each difference was a finding in `known.json` until it was decided. On 2026-11-21 the user chose, for each, the recommendation it was listed with: ten are fixed, so that Lion gives what Scheme gives, in the changes that follow this one, and the ten this record names are departures.
decision: Ten cases stay as they are, as departures from Scheme. A condition is a boolean in `and`, `or`, `not`, and `boolean/not` as it is in `cond` and in a rule's filter, so `(and 1 2)`, `(or #f 3)`, and `(not 3)` fail where Scheme gives 2, 3, and #f. A `cond` case is a condition and one result, written with `begin` when it is a sequence, so every case stays a pair. Forcing a promise while it is being forced fails, as Racket's `force` does, where R7RS gives the first value computed. `func/catch` gives its handler a record of the failure, with what was raised under `value`, so one handler reads every failure the same way, where Scheme's `guard` gives the raised object. A record is a JSON value that never changes: `object/set` gives a new one, as Racket's immutable `hash-set` does, where an R7RS record's modifier changes it. A string's positions and length count UTF-16 code units, as JavaScript's do, for every string function alike, until a decision moves them all to characters together. `array/map` takes one list and the function, data first, and a function that pairs up lists, `array/zip`, serves where Scheme's `map` takes several. A continuation resumes once, since the delimited part runs in a fiber of its own, where Scheme's can resume again.
consequences: The ten cases leave `known.json`: the rule `scheme-racket-semantics` excepts them, and what this record asserts of each is what its probe gives. The other ten wait in `known.json` until the change that fixes each. Lion's list of departures from Scheme grows from one to eleven.

alternatives.option: Give what Scheme gives in all twenty cases
alternatives.rejected: Six of the ten would undo a rule Lion keeps on purpose: that conditions are booleans, that values are immutable data facts can hold, that a catch handler reads every failure the same way, and that a continuation's fiber goes on once.
In the other ten Lion fails or gives a value Scheme does not for no reason of its own, as `(+)` failing while the README says `number/add` works as `+` does.

alternatives.option: Count string positions in characters now
alternatives.rejected: Every string function counts code units, so changing `string/length` alone would make its positions disagree with `string/slice`, `string/indexOf`, and `string/split`; that is a decision for all of them at once.

claims.quote: A condition is a boolean in `and`, `or`, `not`, and `boolean/not` as it is in `cond` and in a rule's filter

says.because: a condition is a boolean in every form alike, as a filter in a rule must be

claims.quote: A `cond` case is a condition and one result, written with `begin` when it is a sequence, so every case stays a pair.

says.because: a result written with begin does the same, and a case that is a pair is what the analysis and the editor read

claims.quote: Forcing a promise while it is being forced fails, as Racket's `force` does, where R7RS gives the first value computed.

says.because: Lion's delay is Racket's, and a promise that forces itself would otherwise loop

claims.quote: `func/catch` gives its handler a record of the failure, with what was raised under `value`, so one handler reads every failure the same way

says.because: one handler reads a raised value and a failure of Lion's own the same way

claims.quote: A record is a JSON value that never changes: `object/set` gives a new one, as Racket's immutable `hash-set` does

says.because: a value is data that facts and answers can hold, and a fact must not change under its relation

claims.quote: A string's positions and length count UTF-16 code units, as JavaScript's do, for every string function alike, until a decision moves them all to characters together.

says.because: every string function counts the same units, and changing one alone would make their positions disagree

claims.quote: `array/map` takes one list and the function, data first, and a function that pairs up lists, `array/zip`, serves where Scheme's `map` takes several.

says.because: a function that pairs up lists serves the same need and leaves array/map's arguments as they are

claims.quote: A continuation resumes once, since the delimited part runs in a fiber of its own, where Scheme's can resume again.

says.because: the delimited part runs in a fiber of its own, which can only go on once

claims.quote: Ten cases stay as they are, as departures from Scheme.

says.statement: Lion's semantics are approximately those of Scheme and Racket, plus the logic layer; each departure is a case a decision names as an exception
